newsitem.title: USA: DSP, Proxim say deal non-dilutive.
newsitem.headline: DSP, Proxim say deal non-dilutive.

text.p: Wireless chip maker DSP Communications said it is confident its merger with Proxim Inc, a maker of wireless computing networking products, will not be dilutive to earnings.
DSP stock tumbled 10-1/4 to 42-1/8, while Proxim's shares rose 6-19/64 to 25 after the firms announced a merger through a tax-free exchange of shares valued at $400 million.

"Analysts estimate that it will be five percent dilutive" in 1997, said DSP chief executive Nathan Hod at an industry conference in Monterey. "Knowing what analysts don't know about DSP, I believe this deal will not be dilutive," he said.
DSPC said it expects to see benefits soon.

"DSPC's Isreali subsidiaries have a very beneficial tax situation and we believe that...some of Proxim's activities will be able to base out of Israel and by doing that we'll be able to get a very significant positive bottom line effect for Proxim," said Gerald Dogon, DSP chief financial officer, said on a conference call after the news was announced.
"That's something we'll be working on in the short term, and we believe that already in 1997 it will start to have positive effects on Proxim," he said.
"I think there's opportunity to either increase the top line or generate more bottom line," said Proxim chief executive David King during the conference call.
Under the deal, Proxim shareholders will get 0.70 of a DSPC common share for each Proxim share. Based on Monday's closing price, the deal values Proxim at $36.66 per share.
David Gilo, chairman of DSP, said the deal contemplates an adjustment based on each company's fourth quarter results.
If either company missed fourth quarter estimates by more than a penny a share, the deal (exchange ratio) would be adjusted, Gilo said.
"If either company missed their numbers, there's a benefit to the other side in a small amount," King added.
Furthermore, if either side misses its fourth quarter estimate by more than $0.03 a share, the deal could be terminated, according to King.

"But neither side anticipates missing the numbers at this point," said King, referring to Wall Street estimates for DSP to earn $0.33 a share in the fourth quarter and for Proxim to earn $0.15 a share in the fourth quarter.
The companies expect to complete the deal after they announce fourth quarter results in January.
